title: Your Dashboard is Not an Agentic OS
description: A dashboard shows you what your agents are doing. An agentic OS manages the system when you're not watching. Session persistence, crash recovery, multi-agent coordination. Here's the difference.
transcript: A dashboard shows you what your agents are doing. An agentic OS manages the system when you're not watching. Session persistence, crash recovery, multi-agent coordination. Here's the difference.

top_comments.author: @TheRealLloydFrazier
top_comments.text:
Hey James, first off, respect where it’s due: you’ve built a genuinely impressive agent setup. There is real work behind what you showed.

That said, one thing you mentioned raised a security flag for me. I’m not saying your system is vulnerable, and I’m definitely not trying to pitch you something in a YouTube comment. I would need to see the actual architecture before making that claim. But based on what you described, there may be risks around agent memory, tool access, prompt injection, persistence, and long-horizon autonomy that are worth pressure-testing before scaling too far.

This is the field I work in. I have nearly 70 patent filings in process, many focused on LLMs, agentic AI, memory systems, orchestration, and security. I’m also launching an autonomous operating substrate designed for true long-horizon operation — not just days or weeks, but continuous operation over years and potentially decades.

Again, I’m not taking a shot at your work. Quite the opposite. You’re far enough along that security architecture really matters now. The stronger the agent, the more dangerous small blind spots become.
